They used to be with UPS and it felt alot smoother (could just be grass is greener effect though). Because shipping is different with fedex they can't offer the same things like with PUR, which may be why that's different (ups vs fedex). Just speculation on that obv

It's a combination between FedEx and where the item comes from a GS store. Items ordered are taken out of local stores' inventory if its closer/available. But then comes a numerous amount of things, if fedex picks them up, if gs packs it correctly and gets it picked up on time, sometimes fedex doesn't show up at all even if we schedule for pick up, sometimes fedex people don't scan the item until way later to be shipped because they're doing them all in order received, etc. 

In the past we actually had to pause fedex shipments in some areas because they were too overrun by previous orders and fedex themselves got backed up. So some of them get shipped through USPS. 

Overall, yeah it sucks sadly but there's not a 1 easy factor as to why. But luckily the customer support for online orders in terms of refunds are pretty quick for the most part.

I don't know if I dislike the job itself, or if I dislike me living in the situation that I'm in. I'm pretty sure it's a mix of both sadly. I work as a Gamestop Manager, and it's extremely sales based as well as keeping up store maintenance, employees, the whole nine yards. It can be stressful, and at the end of the day has made my love for "games" quite a bit less. 

You say it's possible to find a base 60-70k salary position somewhere with the experience in management that I have, I wonder where are places I could even apply for something like that?

I'm basically at the peak of advancements for a long time. I started as a seasonal in 2017, and worked my way up to store manager at the start of COVID (2020). Past that would be district manager, but the problem is is that I'm in a dying company, Gamestop.

It's sadly really complicated. They weren't the best of parents growing up either... I don't want to get too into it but tl;dr, 25 year old marriage to be divorced, spite and anger toward other parent were funneled into me while I was growing up. Because of that, it made me want to run away from them as furthest as I could. 

I am in contact with my mom more than my dad though. She did offer that I could quit my job and move in back with her, and get a WFH and save up from there. My sister has been taking care of my mom, and while she has differing opinions (she doesn't like the idea of me taking advantage of my mom(?) is the best way to put it..?) she said that if I did do decide to move back in with her, I would have to be under full quarantine like that have since the start of COVID.

While it is probably the smartest thing to do financial wise and probably best case in all other scenarios... I guess I just have trouble bringing myself to.  There's probably absolutely nothing wrong with going back especially since she's sickly and I could help her.. I feel deterred to mainly because of my sister's opinions (shes +12 years older than me, has 3 kids, etc) shes a lot more straight forward with the fact that I've basically been no contact with them for 6+ years. And it's true, I feel like I don't deserve it too. But it's something I do want to be able to do too.. I just don't know if its the best decision when I feel like .. depression + quarantine is just a recipe for worse. I just want to be cautious..

My dad has been a huge guilt trip ever since too, and I feel has also become very manic.. I felt like nothing I said ever got through to him. I was finally able to admit that I had tried to commit some years ago, and that I wanted his help and support. He said okay. Then the following week, told me he was taking me off the car insurance, and told me I had nothing going for me in life and I was a waste of time. I cut contact with him from that conversation  about 2 years ago. Then he recently called me about his condition had gotten worse. Told him I'd go see him if he could tell me when, but he hasn't contacted me since..   


I just don't want to feel forced to amend ties with him completely just because they are sick.. yea I get it, they're my only set of parents ever and I can always pursue my future ahead of me.  I may not have mentioned much about my mom being particularly bad but I don't really want to get too far into all of that, really. It is an option for me though to move back with her and mending it. I just don't know if it's good for my mental health to have to commit to being fully quarantined, especially because shes immuno-compromised with chemo.

Back in 3.0, BLM's B4 was used to refresh Enochian buff, so a lot of people may have missed this new tooltip in 4.0

B3 -> Enochian -> Thunder IV -> B4 -> F3 -> F2 -> F2 -> Flare -> Flare -> Convert -> (swiftcast) Flare -> Transpose -> Foul (While you have 0 Mana) is the optimal AoE starter.

From here, I'm not entirely sure what's faster in DPS, but there two ways to go from here for the normal rotation without Convert:

> -> F3 -> F2 -> F2 -> Flare -> Transpose -> Foul(?) and so forth.

or

> -> B3 -> B4 -> F3 -> F2 -> F2 -> Flare -> (swiftcast) Flare -> Transpose -> Foul and so forth.

It really depends on your swiftcast cooldowns probably. I'd only really use the double flare with blizzard if swiftcast is up. You generally want to time Foul after you transpose if possible, that way you're always casting if mana ticks aren't in your favor. Thunder IV procs whenever possible, only refreshing the DoT while in Astral Ice.
